title: Private deployment - ACME weekly sync (2026-05-18)
content:
Attendees: Alex Rivera (owner), Priya Nair (solutions eng), Sam Johnson (ACME infra), Liu Wei (security), Michael Ortiz (SRE).

Goals for this sync:
- Quick status on remaining infra milestones (VPC, DNS, KMS).
- Surface current blockers and owners.
- Confirm cutover plan for canary traffic next Tue (5/26).
- Action items and owners.

Notes / updates (quick):
- VPC peering: ACME network team confirmed routes; peering accepted 5/17. Still waiting on security review of route filters. (Owner: Sam)
- VPN -> Private IPs: initial tunnel up, but intermittent drops observed during 30m load test on 5/16. Logs attached to JIRA-7891. (Owner: Michael)
- KMS/HSM: ACME asked to rotate keys post-deploy; need to validate Redwood KMS integration in customer KMS account. Security asked for IAM role mapping doc. (Owner: Liu)
- NFS mount for model artifacts: mount works but perf inconsistent (timeouts when >8 concurrent pulls). Potentially related to MTU or TCP window settings. (Owner: Priya)
- RBAC and SAML: ACME SSO metadata provided; mapping tested in staging. Need final attribute mapping from ACME IdP. (Owner: Alex)

Blockers (explicit):
1) Security sign-off on VPC route filters - blocks canary (impact: high). Evidence: route table needs explicit deny for 10.0.0.0/8 flows. (Owner: Sam)
2) VPN stability under sustained traffic - blocks autoscaler smoke tests (impact: medium-high). Next step: capture tcpdump during next failure window. (Owner: Michael)
3) KMS role mapping doc from ACME security - blocks encryption verification and final HSM test (impact: medium). (Owner: Liu)
4) NFS throughput - blocks fast model rollouts / cold-start performance tests (impact: medium). Priya investigating mount options + kernel params.

Decisions / agreements from meeting:
- Canary date tentative: Tue 2026-05-26 pending security sign-off and VPN stability. If both not resolved by EOD Mon (5/25), postpone to 6/02. (Decision owner: Alex)
- For KMS, proceed with staged test using temporary CMKs in ACME account to validate flows; HSM rotate to follow. (Owner: Liu)
- Use t2.medium bastion for initial perf debugging (short-lived). Must be removed after troubleshooting window. (Owner: Sam)

Action items (owner / due):
- Sam: Prepare route filter change request and schedule security review by 2026-05-20. Link to change request in JIRA-7891. (due 2026-05-20)
- Michael: Run 2hr VPN soak test tonight, capture tcpdump during failure, upload to JIRA-7891. (due 2026-05-18 EOD)
- Liu: Draft KMS IAM role mapping doc and send to ACME Sec for approval. Include required policy snippets. (due 2026-05-20)
- Priya: Re-run NFS concurrent pull test with updated mount options (noatime, rsize/wsize tweaks) and report perf numbers. Try changing MTU if stable. (due 2026-05-19)
- Alex: Gatekeeper - coordinate with ACME PM to confirm canary window and communicate rollback plan. Prepare runbook for canary (include metrics, abort criteria). (due 2026-05-21)
- All: Add specific rollback steps to the runbook (who flips DNS, who disables peering) and verify with dry-run. (due 2026-05-22)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need ACME to confirm expected RPS for canary (ask Sam). Current test used 150 RPS; ACME expects 200 peak.
- Do we need to provision an additional NIC on the model host for dedicated traffic? Check infra limits.
- Confirm retention policy for logs (ACME compliance wants 13 months). Add to SOW if different.

Quick links/references:
- JIRA-7891 (VPN stability)
- ACME-234 (overall project board)
- Confluence: ACME Private Deployment runbook (link above)
- PR: deploy-scripts/pull/312 (NFS mount fixes)

Next sync: 2026-05-25 10:00 PT (tentative) - goal to sign off final canary prep.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- If route filters delayed: consider isolating canary via separate peering and explicit allow list for canary subnet. Might require extra infra but faster path.
- Keep runbook simple: three abort signals (error rate >5% sustained, latency P95 > 2s, system OOM).
- Remind ACME PM to provide exact SLOs for canary (availability, latency targets).

End of notes.
